title: Add an `athena triage` command that closes done or superseded requests
summary: Add a queue-triage capability so Athena reviews open queued requests against landed jobs and records a disposition (keep, done, superseded, uncertain) with cited evidence. Done and superseded items are closed through the normal close path and logged. Uncertain items are listed for the operator and left open. The audience is the operator, who now does this by hand (OP-17).

defaults_applied.how: Fixture-queue tests plus cargo test and clippy criteria.
Short design note with alternatives in docs/.
Criteria run triage on a fixture and check closures, logging and idempotence.
Checks that done and superseded items end closed with reasons, and live ones stay open.
One focused command reusing the existing close path.
Idempotence and never-close-uncertain are enforced by tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Triage is deterministic and evidence-based: a request is 'done' when a landed job records it as its source, 'superseded' when an explicit supersession link or a later landed job covers it, and otherwise 'keep' or 'uncertain'. No LLM judgment is added in this change.
It is exposed as a new `athena triage` CLI subcommand that reuses Athena::close_with, so closures are logged as Athena actions rather than operator interventions.
Default is a dry-run report; closing happens only with an explicit flag, and uncertain items are never closed.
The role-based requirements engineer is out of scope; this adds only the stage and its acceptance shape.
A short design note goes in docs/ with alternatives, per the designed default.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a fixture-queue test with one done, one superseded and one live request shows the first two closed with a recorded reason citing the evidence (e.g. landing job id) and the live one left open.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows each closure is written through the normal close path as a logged Athena action, not an unlogged intervention.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows running triage twice changes nothing on the second run (no new closures or records).
Run `cargo test`: the triage report lists kept, closed and uncertain items each with a one-line reason, and uncertain items stay open.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean and `cargo test` passes across the workspace.
An operator reading `athena --help` or the docs finds the triage command, its dry-run default, and the disposition vocabulary, and a design note in docs/ lists alternatives considered.
No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) or records/ are changed.

out_of_scope: Changing plan ordering or admission rules
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference because the change adds a new module, a CLI command and fixture tests.
